segments.line: In eight ninety- seven, a pope put a dead man on trial. Not a painting of him. His actual corpse.
And no, this ain't a horror movie. It's in the history books. They call it the Cadaver Synod.
Pope Formosus has been dead for about nine months. The new pope, Stephen the Sixth, really did not like him.
So what does he do? He digs him up.
Dresses the body in full papal robes. And sits it on a throne, in
front of a room full of bishops. Now, a corpse can't talk. So they gave it a lawyer. A young deacon stood behind the throne and answered for the dead guy. The
charge? Breaking church rules to become pope. And you know what the verdict was? Guilty.
Stephen cut off the three fingers Formosus used for blessings and
threw the body in the River Tiber. Like taking out the trash.
But Rome had seen enough. Within months the people turned on Stephen.
He was thrown in prison, and strangled. And
Formosus? Pulled out of the river by a monk, and
buried again, back in Saint Peter's. That's real.
So next time you think your boss holds a grudge, at least he isn't digging you up.
That's about it, folks. Follow for more strange history. See ya!
